en: Wow, really? I can't imagine you'd get fat by doing that.
Well, I also drink lots of black tea, and I'll have sweets to go with it, too.
There's your problem. You wouldn't put on weight if you didn't keep snacking.
Really? So I should try to drink less tea, then?
Yeah. If you need something to drink, try mineral water. Then you're killing two birds with one stone, as far as dieting goes.
Oh, I tried that once before, and it was murder on my stomach.
It's not for everyone. Either way, try to ease up on your tea drinking.
Okaaay.
The tea's not the issue⑬it's the sweets. I don't know what you're eating, but whatever it is, it can't be good.
It's pastries. Like cakes and scones.
Oh, and lately I'm into ice cream too!
You sure eat a lot. How is that "one smallish meal a day"?
Hey, there's always room for dessert! Mainly because I really can't eat much during meals.
You should definitely fix that first, then.
You need to stop right away. Even if you eat small meals, all those sweets are going to make you fat.
For real? Then I guess I'll have to go on a diet. You're a jerk, Kiryu-san.
Hey, you asked.
But it's winter. Doesn't eating ice cream make you cold?
Nah, I sit in the kotatsu, so I'm fine! Nothing beats the happiness of eating something nice and cold while you're comfy and warm!
If you're that self-indulgent, it's no wonder you're having problems.
That's not it. Are you getting enough exercise? Even if you only eat a small amount, you can put on weight if you're not active.
I get enough. The closest train station to my house is a twenty-minute walk, and I make sure not to take a taxi.
That's good. Then the cause must be overeating.
It's dangerous for a woman to walk alone. You should probably take a taxi.
But it'd be a waste of money if I took a taxi every day.
Yes, but a hostess like you attracts a lot of attention. You can never be too careful.
Ha! It's good to know you're seriously concerned about me, Kiryu-san!
But if I do that, I won't get any exercise and then I might get fat.
It's tough to get the balance right in your life.
You need to eat more. It's not healthy if you're not getting three meals a day.
I can't eat that much! Plus, with this job, I can't follow a normal meal schedule like people  can with regular day jobs.
I guess you're stuck then. My meal times get messed up when I work the night shift, too. You just have to make the best of your schedule.
See? I'd like to meet even one hostess who always eats three meals a day.
But then how come you're putting on weight?
Yeah, why indeed?
That's not it. You just have to put as much effort as you can into adopting a healthy daily routine.
That's impossible and you know it! I can't turn down the drinks and snacks my clients order for me, can I?
If I ate three whole meals a day on top of that, I'd be sure to get fat!
You have a point. I wonder if there's anything else you could do.
Oh, that reminds me. Just hear me out, okay?
So I'm not into hosts, but a friend of mine has been crazy about them lately, so I've been going out with her after work sometimes.
You're a good friend. It's like when guys hang out and go to a cabaret club.
Yeah, and drinking alone isn't any fun.
It's definitely great to have conversations over drinks.
Sounds like an expensive friendship. Even if you're just tagging along, it can't be cheap to visit hosts that frequently.
No, it's not like that. If we go and have a few drinks, it's not that different from going to a cabaret club.
Oh really? I guess my impression of hosts is that they're pretty pricey.
It's fine if you don't throw money at them!
I've worked as a host myself.
Really!? But what's that got to do with anything?
Right, you have a point there.
The other day I was out shopping when my friend asked me to go drinking. So I changed my plans and went to the club with her.
And then there was this fish-faced guy at the door who said, "Sorry, but we're fully booked today." I got really upset!
I know the feeling. I get pretty annoyed when I go out for drinks, but the place is too packed to get in.
But that's not the issue!
You should have waited. It's pretty normal for popular clubs to have wait times.
What's his face got to do with it?
Hey now, don't nitpick the little details!
Yeesh.
Anyways, the club was practically empty! There were tons of open tables!
Oh? Why'd they say they were full up, then?
Well, I was in my day clothes, and my makeup wasn't as flashy as my work makeup. They probably thought we didn't have any money.
So they kept you out. Interesting.
Isn't it unbelievable? But whenever I pass by on my way back from work, they're all smiles, trying to wave me in!
That's not right. Some clubs have a dress code, but if you aren't breaking it, they should let you in.
Right!? I'm so angry at them that I haven't been back since!
Our club's policy is pretty relaxed. Sometimes clients show up with ridiculous outfits, and we gossip about them after they leave!
I'll be careful about what I wear, then.
It was your fault. You can't go to a host club in that sort of getup.
What!? But I wasn't planning on going, so what was I supposed to do?
It's the same as with a cabaret club. If you want a staff member to notice you, you need to work on your appearance.
I bet you'd spend a different amount of effort dealing with a student in shorts and a T-shirt than a suited-up businessman with a nice watch.
Well, I... Yeah.
So even if you go on the spur of the moment, you might want to consider changing your clothes before you go.
So then does that mean that you got changed before coming out here today?
Doesn't sound that way to me. How do you normally dress?
Like super normal. If I thought I was wearing something awful, then I wouldn't be this mad about it!
I see. Then that's definitely not okay.
Normal's no good. You do know that host clubs aren't the same as your average neighborhood bar, right?
Host clubs are where women get to experience a temporary bit of extravagance. Showing up in casual wear would ruin the club's ambience.
I guess I hadn't thought of it that way. Come to think of it, I did put more effort into things when I first started going.
See what I mean? If you go with the proper attire, you'll be treated much better.
Okay! I'll show 'em next time!
You're really into that place, aren't you?
Maybe you usually wear too much makeup. If you're a regular, they should've recognized you.
Hey, please stop nitpicking! I'm seriously upset about this!
Oh, and now I'm even more irritated! You would make a bad host, Kiryu-san.
Back on your phone again? Guess you never learn.
Oh, I was just checking an online auction.
An auction?
Yeah, there's this famous brand imported dinnerware set I want, and it's usually very expensive. I was trying to get a good deal.
And I found a really good one, but...
Go ahead and buy it.
Well, it's a little pricier than I budgeted for.
I could buy it for you.
Okay, put in a bid for me.
Okay. How do I do that?
Just log in with your account and enter a bid.
My account?
Wait, you don't even know how this works? The bidding time's almost up! We have to hurry!
No way. If I'm going to buy something for you, I need to see it with my own eyes first.
Is that your way of asking me out on a date?
I mean, it's fine if you don't want to go.
You're a slick one, Kiryu-san! And hey, if you really want to buy it for me, that's fine too.
Guess I might have to.
(Looks like she'll say yes if I ask her out.)
I'm kidding. You can buy that sort of thing yourself. You found something cheap, right?
What? Come on, this isn't the time for making jokes like that!
Oh! The bidding is over! You're awful, Kiryu-san!
Hey, if you were in a rush, you should've said so.
Oh, come on. You pulled out your phone hoping that I'd offer to buy it for you.
Ah, you got me!
You've got a lot of nerve, you know.
So, are you really going to buy it for me?
That's too bad. But you'll find something else.
But I looked so hard for this one! I don't even think there are any others!
So, Kiryu-san, will you buy this for me?
Guess I have to.
No way. You can't expect customers to buy you things just because you asked them to.
Well, of course, but I thought you might be an exception, Kiryu-san.
Aww. That's too bad.
Leave that for later. Now's really not the time to be shopping, don't you think?
But time's about to run out!
What does that mean?
Oh my god, Kiryu-san. It's an auction. The item goes to whoever puts in the highest bid within a set time. Once that time is over, you can't bid anymore.
I see. Then why don't you buy it?
So what? If that's the case, you should have done it sooner.
But I⑬
You aren't trying to extort me, are you?
What!? No, of course not! Geez, could you be any more rude!?
Hm. Still seems suspicious to me.
You know, one of the reasons I'm working so hard as a hostess is so I can repay a car loan.
Wow, you already own a car at your age?
Um, well, not exactly. It's less of a loan and more like, uh, paying off damages.
Damages?
That's completely different! Wait, are you trying to be cute and coy about it or something?
Ugh. Let's just forget about it, okay?
And you expect me to pay? I know this trick. Are you looking for a sugar daddy, or what?
No, that's not it! I've already paid it off, all right? You don't need to worry about that.
Okay, so I borrowed a friend's car and I kind of hit something while I was driving it.
You got into an accident?
What did you hit?
Ugh, don't ask. I don't want to relive that.
Anyways, I've been working my butt off because I had to pay several hundred thousand yen to cover the costs.
Didn't you have insurance?
Well, my friend was actually borrowing the car from someone else, so insurance didn't cover it.
I see. It's your fault for not checking on that before you borrowed it.
But get this! Another girl at the club told one of her clients about it, and he wound up paying off all the damages I owed!
You're lucky. If you were paying it off by yourself, it would have taken a lot of time.
I know, right? I kept the accident a secret from my parents, so I was saving up to pay for it on my own.
Be more careful next time. Cars are handy, but they can be dangerous. You're lucky this was a problem that money could fix.
That's why I don't drive anymore! At least now I don't have to worry about something like that happening again.
That's smart. If you're not confident in your ability to drive safely, you shouldn't be driving at all.
Tell your parents. If you had, maybe they could have paid for you instead of a total stranger.
Get real! The main reason I'm saving up money is so that I don't have to rely on them. If they found out, I don't know how they would've reacted.
Besides, I'm not a kid anymore. I should be able to fix my own problems instead of running to my parents for help.
That's true, but don't do anything to make your parents sad, either.
What are you saving up for now then?
Meh, nothing in particular.
Oh, hey, maybe I can save up to pay for driving school and get my license back!
They took your license away? What kind of accident did you get into?
That seems strange. Does this client have some sort of ulterior motive?
Of course not! Geez, paranoid much?
Then what about this other hostess? Are you two particularly close?
Oh right, that. So, there is a little more to the story.
And what's that?
The amount I owed in damages was actually 600,000 yen, but the amount my coworker got from this guy was 800,000 yen!
Seriously? I thought she sounded awfully nice for someone from Tokyo, but to think she'd do it just to make a profit for herself.
Hey, thanks to her I was bailed out big time! I don't think anything bad about her at all.
Looks like you got away with it this time. You Tokyo hostesses aren't to be messed with, huh?
Unbelievable. So the hostess was the one pulling a fast one on the client.
Right! When I heard that, I was super impressed!
If I ever wind up in that sort of situation, I'm definitely going to talk up the amount of money I need!
That's one impressive scam right there.
Are you from Tokyo, Kiryu-san?
Yeah. I used to live here, but due to some... circumstances, I wound up living in Hakata.
Hakata!? Wow, that's really far away!
Yes. And before that I lived in Okinawa.
